heading: INT. BOXING GYM, BASEMENT OF A BAKERY - NIGHT

units.text: INT. BOXING GYM, BASEMENT OF A BAKERY - NIGHT
Low ceiling.
Flour dust drifts through the light of a single bulb.
The ring is eight feet square, ropes tied with bakery twine.
Heat from the ovens above rattles the pipes.
YELENA, twenty-six, a welterweight with a taped nose, sits on her corner stool, chest heaving.
COACH THANDIWE, fifty, built like a door, kneels in front of her with a water bottle.
Across the ring, KIONA, twenty-four, the challenger, shakes out her gloves.
SVEN, sixty, the referee, in a flour-white shirt, checks his watch.
Look at me. She's dropping her right hand.
units.name: THANDIWE

units.text: I see it.
units.name: YELENA

units.text: Do you? She's tired and she thinks you are too.
units.name: THANDIWE

units.text: She's right.
units.name: YELENA

units.text: She's wrong. Breathe.
units.name: THANDIWE

units.text: Yelena breathes.
Thandiwe squeezes water onto her mouthpiece.
Ladies. Time.
units.name: SVEN

units.text: Thandiwe stands.
Yelena rises.
Across the ring, Kiona waits, bouncing on her toes.
Last round. She comes in, you cut left. She backs up, you let her.
units.name: THANDIWE

units.text: The bell, a dented cake pan struck with a spoon, rings.
